publications.title: An Exploratory Study of Single Channel Surface Electromyography for Hand Gesture Classification
publications.subtitle: Minnesota Undergraduate Research & Academic Journal
publications.description: Accurate hand gesture recognition using surface electromyography (sEMG) typically relies on multichannel sensor arrays and computationally intensive models. This limits practical deployment in low-power and embedded systems. This study investigates the feasibility of classifying ten hand gestures using a single sEMG channel combined with lightweight machine learning architectures. Raw sEMG signals were transformed into a comprehensive feature-based representation, including time-domain, frequency-domain, higher-order-crossing, and relative-intensity features. Feature redundancy was reduced using Pearson correlation filtering and the removal of highly correlated features, while dimensionality-reduction techniques (LDA and PCA) were applied selectively. Three classifiers, a feed-forward neural network (NN), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and a support vector machine (SVM), were systematically evaluated across four experiments. Results demonstrate that combining time and frequency features with Pearson filtering and a compact NN can achieve up to 90 percent accuracy, even with limited temporal and spatial information. These findings highlight the potential of single-channel sEMG systems for cost-effective, low-power gesture-recognition applications.

publications.title: Tackling Tuberculosis: A Comparative Dive into Machine Learning for Tuberculosis Detection
publications.subtitle: MINNESOTA UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH & ACADEMIC JOURNAL
publications.description: This study explores the application of machine learning models, specifically a pretrained ResNet-50 model and a general SqueezeNet model, in diagnosing tuberculosis (TB) using chest X-ray images. TB, a persistent infectious disease affecting humanity for millennia, poses challenges in diagnosis, especially in resource-limited settings. Traditional methods, such as sputum smear microscopy and culture, are inefficient, prompting the exploration of advanced technologies like deep learning and computer vision.The study utilized a dataset from Kaggle, consisting of 4,200 chest X-rays, to develop and compare the performance of the two machine learning models. Preprocessing involved data splitting, augmentation, and resizing to enhance training efficiency. Evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and confusion matrix, were employed to assess model performance. Results showcase that the SqueezeNet achieved a loss of 32%, accuracy of 89%, precision of 98%, recall of 80%, and an F1 score of 87%. In contrast, the ResNet-50 model exhibited a loss of 54%, accuracy of 73%, precision of 88%, recall of 52%, and an F1 score of 65%. This study emphasizes the potential of machine learning in TB detection and possible implications for early identification and treatment initiation. The possibility of integrating such models into mobile devices expands their utility in areas lacking TB detection resources. However, despite promising results, the need for continued development of faster, smaller, and more accurate TB detection models remains crucial in contributing to the global efforts in combating TB.

projects.title: Alzheimer Detection Classification
projects.description: The motivation for the Alzheimer Detection Classification project is driven by a curiosity-driven exploration of learning a new CNN architecture, specifically ResNet50. The goal is to apply advanced deep learning techniques to contribute meaningfully to medical research and improve the early detection of Alzheimer's Disease. The project aligns with the broader trend of utilizing AI in healthcare, providing an opportunity for personal growth and skill development in the realms of medical image analysis and deep learning. Ultimately, the project aims to leverage technology for positive impacts on patient outcomes and advance our understanding of neurodegenerative conditions.

projects.title: Tumor Detection&Classification
projects.description: In this Research Project, my main goal has been to enhance the accuracy of brain tumor identification and classification. I've taken a dataset that contains different types of tumors - Glioma, Meningioma, Normal, and Pituitary - and used a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to analyze it. This work represents a promising step toward harnessing technology to aid in critical medical tasks, ultimately contributing to improved healthcare outcomes and patient well-being.

projects.title: Neural-Network-Number-Classifier
projects.description: In this project, I implemented a neural network (using only vanilla Python and NumPy) that classified 28x28 hand-written numbers. In this project, I learned a lot about the math behind forward and backpropagation and how neural networks learn. With this newly found understanding, I was able to program a neural network with 93% accuracy and minimal loss. The architecture of this project consisted of one input, output, and hidden layer that were all fully connected. Overall, this project was an introduction to deep learning and a stepping stone toward getting an in-depth understanding of implementing a neural network in a real world application.

Baud is building a new chip for accelerated training and inference of large AI models. Training a frontier AI model today takes thousands of GPUs, millions in capex, megawatts of electricity, and sophisticated distributed training infrastructure. This makes it such that only a handful of teams on Earth have a shot at creating frontier-level intelligence for new Opus-like moments in other domains such as robotics, drug discovery, world simulations, material science, and physics. Baud is tackling this by co-designing their chip with a new way to represent neural networks that does not require multiplications during both training and inference. This makes their chip simpler, faster, less power-hungry, and easier to build. Their first chip is validated on the Global Foundries 12nm process and is scheduled for tape-out by the end of this year. They are now taking reservations for their accelerated training service, which is already live on a cluster of FPGAs emulating their chip. Baud is founded by Sarang Z. , who is a multi-time founder with 4 patents and 7+ years in building deep learning hardware, and Eric Taylor , an ex-NVIDIA chip design veteran with 4 tape-outs on leading process nodes and multiple IP releases, patents, and publications. Congrats to the team on the launch! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gexPYcZ8 ...more ...more

We’re 3 weeks away from Y Combinator ’s demo day. We had revenue, raving customers, but decided to pivot from biotech to auto shops. Here’s why: Over the last 12 months, Liam McBride and I built Alchemy , an image analysis platform that builds fast, auditable workflows to answer any technical question about your 2D/3D images. But when we ran The Mom Test Book on directors of major medical clinics, we found that image analysis usually sits buried under a hundred competing priorities (like securing grants), with no real urgency behind it. Liam and I wanted to build a billion-dollar company - fast, and wanted to leverage our experience in multi-modal workflow automation. So we sat down and ranked our potential pivot ideas ( https://lnkd.in/g8JpsNdQ ): • How big it seems • Founder/market fit • How easy to get started • Early market feedback Then, we called everyone in our network to validate/invalidate each idea, landed on auto shops through a personal connection, and then cold-called hundreds more in a single week. Going from biotech to auto shops was a scary transition, but we are confident that 99% of AI use cases lie outside Silicon Valley, and we've already confirmed significantly more traction than we ever saw with Alchemy. More coming soon. ...more ...more

NEW paper from Google DeepMind. (bookmark it) AI Co-Mathematician is an agentic research workbench for mathematicians, and it just hit 48% on FrontierMath Tier 4, a new high score among AI systems evaluated. The system is an asynchronous, stateful environment that supports ideation, literature discovery, computational analysis, theorem verification, and knowledge development. It manages uncertainty, clarifies intentions, records unsuccessful attempts, and emits formal mathematical outputs. Early applications yielded solved open problems, fresh research angles, and recovered overlooked citations during active research sessions. This is one of the cleanest demonstrations that agentic AI moves the frontier on genuinely hard mathematical research, not just problem-solving but discovery support. The asynchronous stateful workbench design is interesting to adopt if you are building agents for any expert workflow. ...more ...more

We built a senior HVAC technician that fits in your earbuds. On-device by default. Works without a signal. You see every time it reaches out. Shipped this weekend at the Gemma 4 Voice Agents Hackathon at YC SF (Cactus × Google DeepMind × Y Combinator). The judging panel included @Andrew Miklas (YC GP). The US is short ~110,000 HVAC technicians. Training a new one takes 3-5 years. Experienced techs close jobs on the first visit far more often than juniors. So we put a senior tech on a chip. The build: Gemma 4 E4B via @Cactus (YC S25) on an M4 MacBook Pro. Three clients, one runtime: Chrome, iPhone Safari, and Rokid Corporation Ltd AR glasses over WebRTC. Audio + vision + function calling in ONE forward pass. No Whisper → ViT → LLM stitching. 6 HVAC tools. 5 on-device + 1 explicit online-escalation with a UI banner. You can see every time it hits the network. The gnarliest engineering problem: Gemma 4 emits three different tool-call opener syntaxes within the same model. Parens, pipes, and a mid-pipe-missing curly form. Raw markers were leaking into every transcript. Built a stateful token sanitizer that buffers partial markers off the wire and emits clean suffixes. Users see clean text. The tool-loop still captures structured calls. Numbers: 217 ms bare-model TTFT, 17 tok/s decode on Gemma 4 E4B. 7/8 tool-match, 100% arg-match on the 8-case benchmark. 18 HVAC KB entries across 10 brands. Keyword retrieval under 1 ms. Direct follow-up to our Feb 2026 FunctionGemma Hybrid Router (2nd place, DC edition). Gemma 4 E4B is ~15× larger and natively multimodal, so most of the 270M-era workarounds disappeared. Built with Tash Matsusaki (Rokid Kotlin app + WebRTC bridge), Amogh D. Prasanna (HVAC tech interviews with Bhuvan R. + Reddit-backed search tool), and Evode Manirahari . Pair-programmed with Claude (Anthropic). For field agents on a rooftop with no signal where do you draw the on-device vs cloud line? I am so happy to introduce Lattices, an open-source research discovery platform that we have developed to visualize scientific literature as a map rather than another ranked list. Lattices retrieves data from OpenAlex, PubMed, zbMATH Open, and arXiv, searching through thousands of research articles across multiple domains. The graph is constructed based on the actual semantic content of the papers: • Every title and abstract is encoded using all-MiniLM-L6-v2. • Cosine similarity finds every paper's closest semantic neighbors. • Papers are first clustered by the era of their publication and then clustered by meaning seeded by K-means. • Cluster names are assigned locally by TF-IDF phrases without any LLM naming the clusters for us. • The newer clusters either link to a semantically similar older cluster or else start their own branch. This results in a chronological research landscape where old themes are closer to the center, new themes spread out, and each paper rotates around its own cluster. Paper similarities are accessible during zoomed-in analysis without overloading the overview. Lattices map semantic similarity and not citation influence, so being connected implies that two papers talk about similar topics, not just that one cites another. The system consists of a Python/FastAPI retrieval and graph pipeline in conjunction with React, TypeScript, Sigma.js, and Graphology interface. It could be executed as a CLI, reusable Python package, local app, and is deployed to lattices.lol via vercel. The hosted version also utilizes ONNX export of MiniLM to maintain efficient semantic inference within a serverless architecture. This was also our team's ( Emmanuel Zhagui-Quito , Nikhil Iyer ) first experience with AI assisted software. We wanted to see if we could turn an idea into a complete, deployed application in under 24 hours. To our surprise this entire venture took under 16! In addition, it taught us a lot about architecture, data structuring, semantic clustering, graph networks, and AI assisted UI design. Try Lattices: https://lnkd.in/ga_-W42Z , lattices.lol GitHub: https://lnkd.in/gzxGvCqg
